title: Adana-Style Spiced Lamb Kebabs with Sumac Onions
summary: Hand-shaped flat skewers of spiced lamb mince, kneaded until sticky and grilled over high heat until charred, served with tangy sumac onions, blistered peppers and tomatoes, and warm flatbread.
equipment: 4 wide flat metal skewers (about 2 cm wide)
barbecue or large ridged cast-iron griddle pan

ingredients.item: small onion, very finely grated, juice squeezed out
Turkish pul biber or Aleppo pepper flakes
ingredients.note: or 1 tsp chilli flakes plus 1 tsp sweet paprika

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
long green peppers (or 2 green peppers, halved)

steps.title: Mix and knead the lamb
steps.text: Put the lamb mince, squeezed onion, garlic, tomato purée, pepper flakes, paprika, cumin, sumac, salt and pepper into a large bowl and knead firmly with your hand for 2-3 minutes, until the mixture turns sticky and starts clinging to the sides of the bowl. Work in the ice-cold water at the end. This hard kneading develops the proteins in the mince so the kebab grips tightly to the skewer instead of crumbling apart on the grill.

steps.title: Chill the mixture
steps.text: Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Chilling firms the fat and lets the kneaded proteins set, which helps each kebab hold its shape once it's on the skewer and over direct heat.

steps.title: Make the sumac onions
steps.text: Rub the thinly sliced red onion with the sumac until it turns pink and softens slightly, then toss with the chopped parsley and lemon juice. The acidity and salt draw out some of the onion's sharpness, leaving a tangy, slightly softened salad rather than a raw bite.

steps.title: Shape the kebabs
steps.text: With wet hands, divide the lamb into 4 portions and squeeze each one around a flat skewer, pressing it into a long shape about 22 cm long and 2 cm thick. Pinch ridges along the length with your fingers, then lay the shaped kebabs on the lined tray. Wet hands stop the sticky mince from sticking to your fingers, and the ridges give extra surface area that crisps and chars on the grill.

steps.title: Grill the peppers and tomatoes
steps.text: Heat the barbecue or griddle pan over high heat until very hot. Brush the peppers and tomatoes with the oil and grill for 6-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until blistered and softened, then set them aside.

steps.title: Grill the kebabs
steps.text: Lay the kebabs on the hot grill and cook for 8-10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes, without moving them until they naturally release from the bars. Look for deep, even browning all over, and check with a probe thermometer that the thickest part reads 71°C, the safe temperature for lamb mince.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Warm the flatbreads on the grill for about 20 seconds, then lay a kebab on each one, sliding it off the skewer by gripping it through the bread. Serve with the sumac onions, grilled peppers and tomatoes alongside.

tips: Knead the lamb mince hard until it turns sticky — this is what makes it cling to the skewer instead of falling apart on the grill; a light mix won't hold its shape.
Squeeze the grated onion to remove its juice before adding it to the mince; too much liquid makes the mixture too wet to shape.
Don't move the kebabs on the grill too soon — let them sear until they release naturally, or the surface can tear and stick to the bars.
Because this is lamb mince, cook it all the way to 71°C at the centre rather than the lower temperature used for whole cuts of lamb.
Wet your hands before shaping the kebabs around the skewers; dry hands make the sticky mixture stick to you instead of the metal.
storage: Cooked kebabs keep in a covered container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat thoroughly until piping hot (74°C) in a hot pan or oven before serving again; the sumac onion salad is best made fresh and doesn't keep well once dressed. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
